title: Two accounts of laws and time
version: Author's draft marked 'to appear Philosophical Studies', 30 PDF pages, SHA-256 5179608983c9aca02333dd5a1d1536c63cf9d9063bc761ddd469442bb1a00333. Published Philosophical Studies 160(1):115-137 (2012); published text not compared.
locator: Draft PDF pp. 3-6 (Sec. II, Maudlin on laws and time), pp. 12-15 (Mentaculus, records), pp. 22-28 (Sec. V comparison, M-arrow objections, Maudlin's petitio reply, conclusion). Pp. 7-11, 16-21 skimmed by search only.
relevance: The best single statement of the Maudlin-versus-Humean standoff on the direction of time. Supplies the target claim tested here: M-arrows are neither sufficient nor necessary for the entropic, epistemic and control arrows (draft pp. 24-25).
limits: Draft, not the published version. Loewer's reconstruction of Maudlin, not Maudlin's text; Maudlin's words appear only as Loewer quotes them. Read through PDFKit text extraction, not page images.
assumptions: Mentaculus = deterministic dynamics + Past Hypothesis + uniform measure over the PH macrostate (pp. 12-13); Maudlin's laws are non-Humean producers whose direction is set by primitive M-arrows, with chances read as propensities (pp. 4-6). Footnote 26 notes that with probabilistic dynamics (GRW) the initial measure need not be posited but the PH still does its work.
conclusion: Loewer judges the dispute a mutual charge of question-begging (pp. 25-26) and prefers the Lewis-Albert view on parsimony (p. 27). He argues M-arrows can point against the entropy gradient, so they are not sufficient, and that a Humean duplicate without them has the same arrows, so they are not necessary (pp. 24-25).
dependencies: Maudlin 2007, The Metaphysics Within Physics, ch. 4 (as quoted)
open_questions: Does the sufficiency objection survive when the M-laws are stochastic and time-homogeneous? Tested in RESULT.md.

title: The Metaphysics Within Physics
locator: Ch. 4 'On the Passing of Time', reached only through Loewer 2012 draft pp. 5-6, 25-26 (quotations, incl. a passage Loewer locates at p. 143) and Healey's NDPR review.
relevance: The main defence of a primitive, law-linked direction of time. The rival this lane reconstructs.
limits: Not read. Every attribution in RESULT.md is to Maudlin as reported by Loewer or Healey. Not in sources-local. Maudlin 2002 'Remarks on the Passing of Time' (Proc. Aristotelian Soc. 102) also unread.

title: The Metaphysics Within Physics (review)

relevance: Second independent report of Maudlin's ch. 4: primitive temporal orientation compatible with a block; statistics needs later states produced from an early microscopically typical state; mention of weak-interaction asymmetry.

title: Does Indeterminism Give Rise to an Intrinsic Time Arrow?
relevance: Nearest precedent: claims genuine indeterminism yields a thermodynamic arrow whatever the initial condition, tested on GRW. RESULT.md's lemma is a finite, conditional relative of this claim.
limits: Abstract only. Their claim is stronger (independent of initial conditions) than anything shown here, and its argument is unread.
